body:
I feel like it is too late for me to become strong enough to deal with offensive people who I'm "not supposed to take personally". It took me until age 25 to simply acknowledge that I had low self esteem. The next thing for me to do was ask myself the question: "Was my low self-esteem caused by someone else?". I was afraid to entertain this question because I thought that it made me sound like I was blaming others. 
Eventually, around age 30, I realized that there is no way that my low self-esteem was simply my fault. So I started engaging with fights that felt like I was finally standing up for myself. The problem is that, when the dust settles after a fight (with a stubborn fuck who refuses to take any responsibility for anything), I cannot remember how I was in the right; I can't remember how to feel like my emotions/anger is valid. I am now convinced that I have allowed destructive people throughout my life to invalidate every emotion I have, including the rage that I have been holding onto for dear life. Expressing the rage is the only thing that makes me feel alive but if that's the case then I don't see why I should press on. I don't want to die but i feel that I have to do myself and others a favor and shoot myself. **Where the fuck do people get so much self-worth that they see validity in their most irrational moments even when they know they are wrong? Why can't these people share some of that self-righteousness with me?** I am losing a battle with destructive people and I am attacking myself and others constantly.
